## Batch 4 step-3 fix pass — report

Reviewing Alpha: group **c** (`research/frontier-18-alpha-c-step3-scaffold-review.md`, `covers: 1, 3, 4`). Verdict on my pair was **insufficient on B4-1 alone**.

**B4-1 — applied.** Alpha is right and I verified both points from disk rather than from the report. `items/cor-principal-ideal-domains-are-noetherian.md` reads `status: published`, `literature-derived` statement, homed on the *A* page `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms` at order 110 against this page's 111.001, inside the declared `requires` closure. My step-2 decline reason was true at 03:45 and is false now. I also re-fetched the H20 snapshot and read the passage: *"From the Hilbert basis theorem (second version) we have at once: Corollary 5.9. A finitely generated algebra over a PID is Noetherian."* The source gives it no proof beyond the citation — exactly the cheap corollary the richness pass should catch.

Added at A-page position 19, directly after `cor-finite-type-algebra-over-noetherian-ring-is-noetherian`:

- `cor-finite-type-algebra-over-a-principal-ideal-domain-is-noetherian`, corollary, "Every algebra of finite type over a principal ideal domain is a Noetherian ring"
- deps: Alpha's three, **plus `def-principal-ideal-domain`** — this is the term's first occurrence on the A page, so the Statement would otherwise use an undefined term. Published, order 50, same closure.

Harvest row re-dispositioned `deferred` → `included`; the false reason and the unreachable destination (a published page that would never have built it) removed. Full contract added to `scope` and `contracts`: two citations, two derivations, all eight boundary rows. Both quotes hand-checked against the cited sections under `proof-contract.mjs`'s own normaliser.

Two things carried to step 5 in the boundary worksheet: a field **is** a PID under `def-principal-ideal-domain`, so this subsumes the field case of `cor-finite-variable-polynomial-ring-noetherian` (that convention goes in the Given line — a corollary gets no Remark section under SCHEMA §4); and the converse is false, `\mathbb Z[x]` being Noetherian but not a PID since `(2,x)` is not principal. `finite_smoke` is empty because no registry check is a bounded countermodel here, and naming one that resolves to nothing is worse than naming none.

**B4-2 — no action, Alpha declined.** The re-fetch confirms both of Alpha's grounds: 5.5 is over a *field*, and its proof turns on "we may assume that $f$ is monic in $x_n$". The `deferred` row to `noether-normalisation-and-nullstellensatz` stands.

**T-1 — recorded, out of my write scope.** Because `validate-plan` skips the order check on a dep already in `items/`, the gate cannot vouch for my two new external edges; I checked them by hand (orders 110 and 50, both A pages, both in closure).

**My twelve step-2 findings:** 1–9 and 11–12 approved as scaffolded, 10 declined (= B4-2). No scaffold edit follows from any; all recorded per-id in the notes.

Consequential edits to my own record: section 1's A-page table is 39 rows renumbered past position 18 with the landmark line moved to match the same ten items; section 2 records the addition, restates items 20/30/34/37 as 21/31/35/38, and reads 39 against the 60 ceiling; section 5 reads 51 ids with the clash check re-run clean.

**Gates, all re-run at final state:** coverage-checklist 1 page / 115 harvested / 0 errors; content-policy `--manifest-only` whole-run 786 items / 0 errors; validate-plan OK; depsource 0 unresolved; prosecheck 0 errors (19 warnings, all count-in-prose inside `notes.md`, which is the report to you, not page prose).

**What is not attested.** `validate-plan` and `depsource` read `plan-spec.json`, which does not carry this batch's items until the step-4 splice — neither has seen the new corollary; they attest the spec is still consistent, not that my new edges resolve. `proof-contract --items` on the new id returns `item-missing`, correctly, since nothing is authored. I did not touch `plan-spec.json` (its modified state predates this dispatch), any other batch, `items/` or `library/`. The whole-run content-policy count moved 785 → 786 between two runs from another batch's concurrent edit, not mine; my batch is 39 + 12.
